headline: Human Neuronal UNC13A Cryptic-Exon Blockade Restores Evoked Synaptic Release
prior_state_or_assumption: Preclinical UNC13A (EALS-001) steric-ASO validation rested on iPSC motor-neuron splicing and Munc13-1 protein recovery (Brown 2022 PMID:35197628; Ma 2022 PMID:35197626) without defining the quantitative human protein threshold required to rescue evoked synaptic transmission.
new_evidence_or_revision: Keuss et al. (2026, Nature, PMID:43015463, DOI:10.1038/s41586-026-11256-2) demonstrated that restoring >30% human UNC13A protein via Intron-20 cryptic-exon deletion (~75% protein rescue) or 2'-O-MOE ASOs rescues miniature and evoked AMPA EPSCs and MEA network synchrony across human cortical and spinal motor neurons. headline: Stoichiometric PIKfyve–PI(3)P–LRRK2/CASM Coupling Narrows Pulsed Apilimod Window
prior_state_or_assumption: Intermittent pulsed PIKfyve inhibition (EALS-020) models typically assume an occupancy dead-zone before endolysosomal vacuolation onset (~79% parameter-grid pass rate) without accounting for immediate +PI(3)P-driven LRRK2/CASM stress coupling.

(2026, Life Sci Alliance, PMID:42994990) demonstrated direct, threshold-free PIKfyve -> +PI(3)P -> LRRK2 Rab10-pThr73 / ATG16L1 CASM recruitment alongside Drosophila C9orf72 secreted DPR data (DOI:10.64898/2026.11.09.765393).
